models_evaluated: Logistic regression model for extended length of stay in AMI (Magalhães et al.)

links.outcome: Discrimination of previously developed model on new hospital's historical data against reference outcome
links.effect: On new-hospital data the model's AUC fell from 0.828 to 0.702 and recall from 72% to 58%; specificity 75% to 73%, showing worse local performance than original evidence.
links.quote: According to the data presented in Table 3 , there is a decrease in the predictive capacity of the VM compared to the results obtained in the model by Magalhães et al. ( 13 ).

links.outcome: Performance after local recalibration versus unadjusted model
links.effect: Recalibrating on local data improved AUC from 0.702 (VM) to 0.745 (RM) and recall from 58% to 69%; Hosmer-Lemeshow p=0.692; specificity fell from 73% to 68%.
links.quote: Regarding the performance measures for the population of patients with AMI who were discharged alive, the results obtained in the RM were worse compared to the validation by Magalhães et al. ( 13 ) and improved compared to the VM (expected result, since the model was adjusted to the population).

links.outcome: Generalizability of model developed at small hospital to larger hospital population
links.effect: Model developed on a ~400-bed hospital did not generalize to a ~1,000-bed hospital in a different period; AUC dropped 0.828 to 0.702 and predictor ORs and CIs differed.
links.quote: Therefore, it highlights the need to recalibrate the models to new populations, as the models cannot be generalized to different populations without losing their predictive capacity.

links.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new population/context
links.effect: Prior model applied to a new population lost predictive capacity (AUC 0.828 to 0.702; recall 72% to 58%), requiring recalibration.
links.quote: As a result, the model required recalibration in the population under study.

links.effect: Recall 72% to 58%; specificity 75% to 73%; AUC 0.828 to 0.702.

links.effect: Previous model could not be generalized; VM AUC 0.702 versus original 0.828.
links.quote: This study allowed researchers to conclude that a previous model for predicting LOSE on patients diagnosed with AMI could not be generalized.

links.effect: Recall improved 58% to 69% and AUC 0.702 to 0.745; specificity decreased 73% to 68%.
